Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a classic CX-MS (Chemical Cross-Linking Mass Spectrometry) study to map protein-protein interactions (specifically autoinhibition of TCPTP). While not a traditional 'enrichment' like phospho-enrichment, it uses cross-linkers to target specific distance-constrained residues. The base workflow is DDA LFQ as no multiplexing labels were used.

scope: We mixed purified full-length TCPTP with increasing concentrations of cross-linker.

TCPTP (0.5 μM) and complex mixture of TCPTPCAT (residue: 1–288) & TCPTPTail (residue: 289–387) at 1:100 and 1:200 ratio (TCPTPCAT −0.75 μM while TCPTPTail - 75 or 150 μM) were mixed with cross-linker BS3 (Bissulfosuccinimidyl suberate) or DSSO (Disuccinimidyl sulfoxide)

Purified TCPTP (0.5 μM) and complex mixture of TCPTP_CAT (residue: 1-288) & TCPTP_Tail (residue: 289-387) at 1:100 and 1:200 ratio (TCPTPCAT -0.75 μM while TCPTPTail - 75 or 150 μM) were mixed with cross-linker BS3 (Bissulfosuccinimidyl suberate) or DSSO (Disuccinimidyl sulfoxide)

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was performed on purified recombinant TCPTP protein and a reconstituted complex of its catalytic domain and C-terminal tail. No subcellular fractionation of a cellular lysate was performed for the MS experiments.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The study primarily uses biochemical assays and CX-MS to investigate autoinhibition. The MS component (CX-MS) is used to map interactions between the catalytic domain and the tail in both full-length TCPTP and reconstituted complexes (TCPTPCAT + TCPTPTail), serving as a structural validation of the genetic and ligand-based perturbations.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) was used on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos for cross-linking analysis; no labeling (SILAC/TMT) is mentioned.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: Explicit use of BS3 and DSSO cross-linkers for both intra- and inter-molecular cross-linking mass spectrometry (CX-MS).
